world.h: LIVE: Tehran says US 'defeated' and cannot dictate peace terms
world.b: Iran says the United States has been "defeated" in the war and cannot dictate the terms of a peace deal. Follow Al Jazeera's live coverage.
world.title: Iran says two more tankers ablaze near Hormuz after hitting mines

world.h: Iran says it shot down two US drones over Hormuz
world.b: Iranian forces say they downed two US drones over the Strait of Hormuz as the United States steps up its economic pressure campaign and efforts to end the war remain stalled.

world.h: Honduras court convicts four, including three Americans
world.b: A court in Honduras convicted four people, three of them US citizens, of criminal association in connection with the 2022 disappearance of a woman whose whereabouts are still unknown.

world.h: Houthis fire three missiles at Riyadh
world.b: The coalition said it intercepted the ballistic missiles Saturday, two days after a Houthi strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower, Riyadh's tallest skyscraper.

national.h: Jury convicts man of starting the Palisades Fire
national.b: After an earlier mistrial, jurors convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of arson for lighting the Jan. 1, 2025, fire that flared up days later into the Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people in Los Angeles and Malibu.

national.h: Trump's proposed arch could shadow Arlington cemetery
national.b: President Trump's proposed 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery could shade gravesites, disrupt visits with construction noise and alter the capital's historic landscape, families of the fallen worry.

national.h: Army plans detonations of degraded explosive in Iowa
national.b: The US Army plans two controlled detonations at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant to destroy 68 drums of degraded lead azide, a volatile lead-based explosive, under an emergency EPA permit.

national.h: Storms on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving travel
national.b: Severe weather is expected on both US coasts next week. San Francisco's mayor urged residents to avoid nonessential travel as the city prepares for extreme high tides and rain.

national.h: FBI investigating apparent hack of national crime database
national.b: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center, the database police use for records on fugitives, missing persons and criminal history, a person familiar with the matter told the AP.

national.h: Witness disputes Texas account of a troubled execution
national.b: Texas defended its execution of 70-year-old Reinaldo Dennes, who pleaded "Don't let me suffer like this" during a lethal injection that followed a struggle to find a vein. His spiritual adviser described severe distress in the Huntsville death chamber.

politics.h: Intelligence chief defends Trump calling Putin a 'friend'
politics.b: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said it was "entirely appropriate" for President Trump to call Vladimir Putin his friend, after last week's three-way summit with Putin and Xi Jinping in China.
politics.title: U.S. intelligence chief says Trump's description of Putin as a 'friend' is 'entirely appropriate'

politics.h: Democrats clinch largest House majority since 1992
politics.b: House Democrats have won at least 258 seats, gaining 44 so far, their best general election result in decades and four more seats than they picked up in 2018.
politics.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, the largest since 1992

politics.h: Christian nationalists see GOP losses as a chance to supplant MAGA
politics.b: Christian nationalists who celebrated Trump's return now see the Republican Party's recent election losses as an opportunity to replace his MAGA movement with their own extremist vision.
politics.title: Christian nationalists see GOP midterm losses as opportunity to supplant Trump's MAGA

politics.h: Trump orders contractors to consult White House on Congress requests
politics.b: A new executive order directs federal contractors to consult the administration about inquiries from Congress and withhold communications the White House deems privileged, or risk losing their contracts.

politics.h: Trump says he would work with Democrats to cap card rates
politics.b: President Trump said he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates, a 2024 campaign promise. The standard proposal caps rates at 10%, against a median of about 22.2%.

international.h: Poland says Russia also targeted Ukrainian American rapper
international.b: Polish authorities say the Ukrainian American man Denmark says it saved from an alleged Russian murder plot was also targeted by Moscow's intelligence services last summer in Poland. Denmark has expelled a Russian official.
international.title: Poland says Russia allegedly twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper

international.h: Lebanese villagers return to homes wrecked during Israeli occupation
international.b: As the Israeli army pulls back in southern Lebanon, families in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah are returning to find homes they say Israeli forces demolished after the US-brokered ceasefire.
international.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back

international.h: Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriots as Russian strikes kill 7
international.b: Russian attacks killed seven people in Ukraine, including in Dymer in the Kyiv region, as President Zelenskyy urged the US to release Patriot missiles.
international.title: Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriot missiles as Russia kills 7 in Ukraine

international.h: Drone attacks kill four around Khartoum, damage UN building
international.b: Drone attacks blamed on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum and damaged a United Nations building, according to local reports and UN officials.
international.title: Drone attacks kill four near Sudan’s capital, damage UN building

international.h: Russian vessel hit by suspected sea drone at Benghazi base
international.b: A suspected sea drone attack hit a Russian vessel at a naval base in eastern Libya, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to Libya's eastern-based government.
international.title: Russian vessel hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Libya’s Benghazi port

international.h: COP31 climate talks in Antalya end without a deal
international.b: The UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday without an agreement after disagreements over fossil fuels, and delegates called the outcome disappointing.
international.title: ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal

international.h: Settlers attack Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank
international.b: Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian towns and villages in the central occupied West Bank, including Kafr Malik, burning cars and damaging property.
international.title: Israeli settlers attack several Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank

international.h: Russian cargo ship still burning off Finland after drone strike
international.b: Fire aboard the Sparta II, struck by drones Saturday off Finland's coast, burned through the night, the Finnish coastguard said. Finland's military says Ukraine likely carried out the strike; the 16 crew were evacuated.

international.h: Indonesia candy factory fire kills three, 36 missing
international.b: A fire at the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province, which borders Jakarta, killed three people and left 36 missing. At least 15 people were rescued, and crews were still fighting the blaze Sunday.

international.h: Displaced Palestinians protest Israeli strikes in Gaza
international.b: Hundreds of displaced Palestinians living near the "Yellow Line" in Gaza demonstrated Saturday as Israeli forces continued air strikes and destroyed buildings beyond the ceasefire line.

international.h: Eleven killed in Sinaloa operation to capture cartel boss
international.b: Mexico's Defence Ministry said seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the overnight operation in Sinaloa that captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

international.h: Bahrain says Iranian attack set industrial site on fire
international.b: Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted a number of Iranian aerial attacks late Saturday, and one struck a civilian industrial facility, starting a fire. Preliminary reports pointed to no injuries.

international.h: Mexico arrests alleged cartel boss 'Chapo Isidro'
international.b: Mexican special forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list, along with two other men in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night, Mexico's defence ministry said.

international.h: India's opposition youth wing protests at Meta offices
international.b: The Indian Youth Congress protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram, demanding the company restore its leaders' Instagram accounts. The protests led to clashes with police and security guards.

international.h: Israeli strike on food aid van kills three in Gaza City
international.b: An Israeli strike on a van carrying food aid west of Gaza City killed three people, part of attacks that killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza despite last year's ceasefire, as winter flooding deepens the crisis.

international.h: Toxic liquor kills at least 11 in India's Manipur
international.b: At least 11 people died after drinking suspected spurious alcohol in northeast India's Manipur state, and more than 180 had been admitted to hospitals as of Friday. Authorities have opened an investigation.

international.h: Geneva talks agree to keep working on 'killer robot' rules
international.b: At a UN conference in Geneva, 128 countries agreed to "elaborate" on a possible accord regulating lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years, after nearly 100 nations pushed for swift, legally binding rules.

international.h: Fire at power station near Basra kills at least four
international.b: A fire broke out at the Hartha power station north of Basra in southern Iraq, killing at least four people and injuring 35, according to Iraqi state media.

business.h: How a small-business loan became a seven-year nightmare
business.b: Merchant cash advances are America's fastest-growing source of small-business funding and one of the least regulated. NPR follows Vahe Shahinian's seven-year fight over a deal he alleges was fraud.
business.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare

business.h: Paolo Bulgari, who built a global jewelry brand, dies at 89
business.b: Paolo Bulgari, grandson of a Greek silversmith, helped turn the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand. His family announced his death Saturday, calling him "the greatest jeweler of our time."
business.title: Paolo Bulgari, who turned a family jewelry business into a global brand, dies at 89

business.h: Judge approves Bayer's Roundup settlement worth up to $7.25 billion
business.b: A Missouri judge gave final approval to Bayer's nationwide settlement with people who say the weed-killer Roundup caused their cancer, a deal that could cost the company up to $7.25 billion.

business.h: Bessent says no new limits needed on Nvidia chip sales to China
business.b: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said no further restrictions on sales of older Nvidia chips to China are needed, after the administration moved this week to block China's remote access to the latest semiconductors.

business.h: Critics say Anthropic's IPO will test its safety pledge
business.b: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq this week, and critics say its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will now be tested as a public company.
business.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?

business.h: AI stocks slump in one of Wall Street's worst weeks in a while
business.b: AI-related stocks and the broader market were pummeled this week, with investors fearing a sector bubble could be bursting. Anthropic's market debut failed to provide the hoped-for lift.
business.title: The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms

science.h: Halted research funds strain trust in Black communities
science.b: Scientists are fighting to restore halted grants, including for Alzheimer's research in a historically Black part of Pittsburgh, where participants took memory tests and shared their stories. Rebuilding trust may be harder.
science.title: Scientists are fighting for their halted funds. Trust of Black communities may be harder to win back

science.h: Two spacecraft slip into orbit around Mercury
science.b: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise. The two linked probes will separate next month to study the planet from different altitudes.

science.h: Why recent tech failures felt connected to so many people
science.b: Outages hit Microsoft, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and government systems such as the FAA and National Weather Service in quick succession. The piece looks at why that pile-on felt coordinated to many people.

science.h: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted Riemann proof
science.b: Levent Alpoge, a mathematician at Anthropic, wrote that he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis working with Claude.

science.h: How much should climate plans lean on carbon capture?
science.b: ProPublica spoke with three leading climate modelers about the assumptions behind models that count on capturing and storing carbon, a technology ProPublica calls unproven.
science.title: Why Is the World Still Counting on Unproven Carbon Capture Technology?

sports.h: Prochazka meets Stirling in UFC main event in Qatar
sports.b: Former light heavyweight champion Jiri Prochazka faces rising star Navajo Stirling in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar. Stirling is seeking his fourth win of 2026.

goodnews.h: Kids in Johannesburg's Alexandra township publish their own book
goodnews.b: Children in the Read Alex literacy program in Johannesburg wrote a new book of short stories drawn from their own lives, From Gomora to the World.
goodnews.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa

local.h: Aber Kawas becomes first Palestinian in New York state Senate
local.b: Aber Kawas won election as the first Palestinian in New York Senate history, celebrating with hundreds of Democratic Socialists of America members on election night.
local.title: Aber Kawas becomes first Palestinian in New York state Senate history

local.h: Jersey City rent control push ends in setback for DSA members
local.b: A bill from progressive Jersey City council members to protect tenants of a waterfront high-rise from rent hikes was tossed before it could be formally introduced.
local.title: A rush to rent control in Jersey City ends in a setback for DSA council members

local.h: Homeless man charged with murder in Chinatown killing
local.b: Police charged a homeless man with murder after a 62-year-old woman was found dead with signs of trauma to her neck at her Catherine Street apartment on Friday.
local.title: NYPD charges homeless man with murder after woman, 62, was killed at Chinatown apartment

local.h: FDNY leaders on lithium-ion fires and EMS shortages
local.b: Fire deaths have nearly doubled since last year, many driven by lithium-ion batteries, and EMS response times remain at a record high. FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore discussed the department's response on WNYC.
local.title: FDNY grapples with lithium-ion danger, EMS shortages and a building collapse

local.h: National Grid gas rate freeze approved, but costs may follow
local.b: State regulators approved a yearlong rate freeze for nearly 2 million National Grid gas customers in the city and on Long Island, but customers will still be on the hook for capital spending during the freeze.
local.title: New York approves National Grid rate freeze, but customers could see higher bills soon

local.h: Judge keeps man shot by ICE in the Bronx in custody
local.b: A federal judge ruled Oscar Belgal, wounded when federal agents fired on his SUV in the Bronx in October, will stay in custody while the administration pursues his deportation.
local.title: Federal judge in NY denies release of man shot by ICE in the Bronx

local.h: Rain returns Sunday, and another storm may hit Thanksgiving
local.b: Showers arrive Sunday afternoon and may linger into the Monday commute, with an inch or two of rain expected across the city. Forecasters are already watching a second storm near Thanksgiving.
local.title: Rain once again coming for NYC's idyllic fall — and maybe Thanksgiving, too

periods.text: A 30 percent chance of rain, mainly before 10pm.  Cloudy, with a low around 56. Northeast wind 6 to 11 mph becoming west after midnight.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, then gradually becoming sunny, with a high near 64. West wind 7 to 16 mph.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 44. Northwest wind 11 to 18 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 49. North wind 11 to 15 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 39.

periods.name: Wednesday
periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 50.

localgood.h: Adopt a storm drain? Council bill would enlist New Yorkers
localgood.b: A City Council bill would let residents volunteer to clear leaves and litter from storm drains on their block, building on a pilot in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, to help prevent flooding.
localgood.title: Adopt a storm drain? NYC proposal aims to enlist residents in flood prevention.
